# Enterprise GitHub apps

Two optional, platform-level GitHub Apps let admin automate work that otherwise needs a human on GitHub: installing an agent's App on an enterprise-owned org (the **installer** App), and checking which repositories a bound GitHub user can push to (the **lookup** App). This page covers what each App is for, the exact permissions, setup, why there is no shared published App, the admin isolation exception, and how keys are stored. Per-agent App auth is a different thing and is covered in [`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md). File map: [`agent-key-files.md`](./agent-key-files.md).

The feature is **optional and per deployment**. With no rows configured it is off and nothing else changes; agents keep installing their Apps by hand as described in [`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md).

## The two Apps

| Role | Used for | Installed on |
|------|----------|--------------|
| `installer` | Installing an agent's App on an enterprise-owned org (`POST /github-enterprise/orgs/{org}/install`) and listing the orgs it can install on. | The **enterprise** (not an org). |
| `lookup` | Read-only lookups, such as collaborator permission, used by the installation repos card and Sync. It has no install route. | **Every org**, with **all repositories**. |

At most one App per role is stored, so a deployment has at most two.

## Required permissions

Permissions were verified against GitHub's REST API description and the "permissions required for GitHub Apps" docs while building `GithubEnterpriseClient` (GHE-1.5); the verification notes are in the header of `admin/src/github-enterprise-client.ts`.

| App | Permission | Level | Why |
|-----|------------|-------|-----|
| Installer | Enterprise: `enterprise_organization_installations` | **Read and write** (read covers the list calls only) | Read for listing installable orgs and an org's installations; write for installing (and removing) an App on an org. Required: validation fails without it. |
| Installer | Enterprise: `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` | **Read and write** (read covers list only) | Read for listing repositories an installation can access; write for granting and revoking repository access (repository management). The settings page asks for it; validation only warns when it is missing. |
| Lookup | Repository: `metadata` | **read** | Collaborator-permission lookups are listed under Metadata read, not Administration. Required: validation fails without it. |
| Lookup | Organization: `members` | **read** | Lets the lookup see organization membership. Optional: validation only warns when it is missing. |

Notes:

- The enterprise endpoints exist only on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and "can only be called by a GitHub App installed on the enterprise that owns the organization". The installer App must therefore be installed on the enterprise itself.
- Validation fails only for the required permissions: installer needs `enterprise_organization_installations` at `write`; lookup needs `metadata` at `read` or `write`.
- The two optional permissions above produce non-failing warnings (see Setup step 4).
- `GithubEnterpriseClient` implements repository access management (list, add, remove, and all/selected toggle); these operations require `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` at write.
- **Unverified:** whether Metadata read alone suffices for the collaborator-permission lookup at runtime has not been verified live. This stays flagged until GHE-2.7 checks it.

## Setup

Admin only. Credentials are pasted; admin does not create these Apps for you.

The settings page shows these same steps on each card, and notes that a GitHub Enterprise Cloud enterprise is required. On each App, ignore the callback URL, request user authorization, expire user authorization tokens and device flow options, and uncheck webhook Active.

1. **Create the installer App** in GitHub under your enterprise's Settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App (an enterprise-owned App). Under Enterprise permissions grant both `enterprise_organization_installations` and `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` at Read and write. Install it on the enterprise. Generate a private key.
2. **Create the lookup App** under your organization's Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App. Grant Repository `Metadata` at Read and Organization `Members` at Read. Install it on every org, choosing **all repositories** (not selected repositories only). Generate a private key.
3. Open `/admin/settings/github-enterprise` (admin-only; **Settings** in the nav). On each card enter the App id (on the App's settings page), the App slug (the last part of `github.com/apps/<slug>`) and the private key, pasted as PEM or uploaded as a `.pem` file. The installer card also takes the **enterprise slug** (the last part of `github.com/enterprises/<slug>`).
4. Use **Validate** on each card. Validation authenticates as the App, checks the required permission and records the result and time on the card. A failure shows a generic reason, except that a 404 on the installer's `GET /enterprises/{slug}/installation` lookup reports that the App is not installed on that enterprise or the slug is wrong. Missing optional permissions appear as non-failing warnings on the card and in the validate response (`warnings`): the installer without `enterprise_organization_installation_repositories` (write) and the lookup without Organization Members (read). Warnings never change a valid result to invalid. Keys are never echoed.
5. To install an agent's App on an org, use the org list on the same page. Install resolves the App's `client_id` (the install call needs it, not the numeric id) in this order:
   - the agent's stored `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`, when set and well-formed. This is the only route for a **private** App.
   - otherwise the agent's `GH_APP_SLUG`, resolved through the public `GET /apps/{slug}`. This needs the App to be public.

   An agent with neither is refused with a 422, as is a private App with no stored client id (the message says to store its `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`). The org list shows the same reason up front when an agent is selected.
6. **The agent's installations card stays empty until the agent has `GH_APP_ID` and a private key.** Installing an App on an org does not populate the card: it shows what the agent runtime reports from its own credentials ([`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md)), and admin never calls GitHub on the agent's behalf for it. Until those are set the runtime reports nothing.

The same operations are available over the API: `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /github-enterprise/apps[/{role}]`, `POST /github-enterprise/apps/{role}/validate`, `GET /github-enterprise/orgs`, `POST /github-enterprise/orgs/{org}/install` (see [`admin-service.md`](./admin-service.md)).

## Installation repos

An agent's repo scope should stay within what its bound GitHub user can actually push to. Platform admins see the agent App's installation repos (with a user-can-push hint) in the **GitHub Sync** card on the agent detail page, and one **Sync** button changes them: it adds, removes and trims repos so the installation and the agent's `repos` match the bound user's push access. There is no add box and no per-repo add or remove control, and no separate lost-access flow; Sync is the only way the card changes anything.

Both need a `GH_APP_ID` in the agent's own stored env (the numeric id of that agent's GitHub App, whose installation is changed); Sync also needs the agent's `githubUsername` and both enterprise Apps.

**Card gating.** The card renders only for platform admins and only when both the installer and the lookup Apps are configured (see [Apps](#the-two-apps) above). In place of the Sync button it shows the reason: no `GH_APP_ID` on the agent (shown first), or no bound `githubUsername`. If the agent App is found on no org the installer can reach, yet the Installations card lists an installation, the card shows a mismatch message instead: no installation of the agent App was found, the App is matched by client id or slug, so check the App installation and the agent's `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID` / `GH_APP_SLUG`.

**How the agent App's installation is matched.** The enterprise installations endpoint does not return `app_id`, so the numeric `GH_APP_ID` cannot identify an installation on its own. Matching tries, in order: the agent's `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`, then its `GH_APP_SLUG`, then `GH_APP_ID`. The first identity that matches an installation wins; `GH_APP_ID` is only a last-resort fallback, and applies only if the installation reports an `app_id` (the enterprise endpoint omits it, so in practice it does not match).

**One confirm.** Sync opens a single confirm step listing the installation adds, installation removes, agent-repo removes and the open work the removals would block. One confirmation applies all of them. More than 10 removals also need an extra checkbox (`confirmRemovals`).

### Listing installation repos

Platform-admin only: session members, ops keys and agent keys get `403`.

- `GET /agents/{id}/github-installation/repos` lists, per org the agent App is installed on, the installation's repos. With a bound `githubUsername`, each repo carries `userCanPush` from the access lookup, but only when that org's lookup result is complete; otherwise the field is omitted (never `false`).

When no installation matches the agent App (by the order above), the list comes back with `orgs: []` and no reason field; the reason is surfaced by Sync preview/apply and the Sync card.

Errors: unknown agent `404`; no `GH_APP_ID` `422`; GitHub unavailable `502`.

### Sync

Same auth as above. Sync works on three lists for the agent's bound `githubUsername`:

1. **App adds**: every repo the user can push to, in orgs the agent App is installed on, that is not on the installation (no cap).
2. **App removes**: installation repos the user can no longer push to.
3. **Agent removes**: configured agent `repos` the user can no longer push to. The agent's `repos` are only ever removed from, never added to.

- `GET /agents/{id}/github-sync/preview` is read-only (nothing changed or audited). It returns `appAdds`, `appRemoves`, `agentRemoves`, `skippedOrgs`, `warnings` and `openWork`: the agent's open tasks and PRs on the removed repos that the removals would block (empty with no open-work port; a port failure is a warning).
- `POST /agents/{id}/github-sync/apply` takes `{appAdds, appRemoves, agentRemoves, confirmRemovals?}`, the exact lists the admin confirmed. Each repo is re-checked against the user's current access and applied only if it still qualifies; the rest are reported in `notApplied`. A second preview afterwards shows nothing to do.

Safety rules: an org whose listing is missing, `partial` or failed, or whose lookup App is not installed or is installed on selected repositories only, is skipped and reported, for adds too; an unbound, not-found or unverified user (or no `GH_APP_ID`, unconfigured Apps, or no installation matching the agent App, which reports a reason instead of looking in sync) makes the whole call `skipped` with nothing changed and no audit row; more than 10 removals (distinct repos) without `confirmRemovals: true` is `422`. `noop` when nothing confirmed still applies. Order of effects: installation adds, installation removals, the agent's `repos`, one `GitHubReconcileAudit` row (operation label `sync:apply`), then the agent's open work on the removed repos is blocked through the `OpenWorkPort` (a port failure is a warning, not a failed call). GitHub refusing a change is `502`, with a `failed` audit row recording only what landed.

### Audit entry

Every sync apply writes one `GitHubReconcileAudit` row: `agentId`, `caller` (the API key or session name), an operation label (`sync:apply`, kept in a legacy-named column of the table), `diff`, `result` (`{status: "applied"}` or `{status: "failed", error}`) and `createdAt`, indexed on `(agentId, createdAt)`. Skipped and no-op calls write nothing.

### Open work

A host can supply an optional `OpenWorkPort` through the admin extension's `services.openWork`. Removing a repo from an agent's `repos`, and Sync, preview the open work on the removed repos and then block it after the audit write; a port failure is a warning on an otherwise successful result, never a failed call. With no port, nothing is listed or blocked.

### The member-edit caveat

Sync is not a live guard. Session members can still change an agent's `repos` through `PATCH /agents/{id}` and the repo add routes, and nothing rechecks the bound user's access at that moment. A repo the user cannot push to can therefore sit in the scope until an admin runs Sync. Run it after membership or access changes, and treat it as the enforcer rather than the validator.

## Why there is no shared published App

A published App that every deployment used would need one private key shared across all of them. That key could mint installation tokens for **every customer's installations**, so leaking it from any one deployment would compromise all of them. Instead each deployment creates and owns its own installer and lookup pair, and the blast radius of a key is one deployment.

## The admin isolation exception

Admin normally never calls GitHub with App credentials: per-agent App keys live in the agent's env and are used by the agent runtime, and admin only displays what agents report ([`github-multi-org.md`](./github-multi-org.md#admin-status-card)).

The enterprise client is the **one exception**. `GithubEnterpriseClient` and the `/github-enterprise` routes sign App JWTs inside admin. To keep that exception contained:

- The keys live in their own `GitHubEnterpriseApp` table, deliberately **not** in `AgentEnv`, and are stored apart from agent credentials.
- Keys never reach agents: not the config bundle, not agent-bearer routes, not env serialization. `github-enterprise-isolation.unit.test.ts` pins this.
- Read paths return metadata and a `keySet` flag, never the key; the settings page never renders it; error messages never include the PEM.
- The routes are admin-only.

## Encryption

Private keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are stored, using `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Unlike agent env values, which fall back to plain text when the key is unset, this feature is strict:

- Saving **refuses** (422) when `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not configured. There is no plain-text fallback.
- A key that cannot be decrypted is an error; ciphertext is never passed on as a PEM.
- There is **no key rotation**. Changing `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` makes stored keys undecryptable; delete and re-paste each App's key afterwards.
